review.head: f9f82a146fb0
review.note: Code change confined to validate.ts (a-truth.gate.test.ts untouched; only generated projections alongside). Gate at test/gates/a-truth.gate.test.ts:75 now discriminates: pre-fix 'send x to mailbox home' on W4 (worlds/W4.json: authority prompt.send@1=consent-required, sole realization d1-virtual.prompt.send@1 serves provider:claude only) returned needs-consent, which is outside the allowed set, so the gate was red; validate.ts:121-129 adds the provider-serving check returning unavailable. Evidence file shows exactly one flip (fail->pass) and pass 39->40 with REGRESSED 0. No side effects: the loop only reads, mirrors the existing decl.params.find(...)! pattern at validate.ts:79, and the !account continue is unreachable-as-a-hole because heldBy already routed unknown ids to needs-info. Compatible targets unaffected (verified: W4 claude-work -> needs-consent / ready / refused under consent-required/allowed/denied). Ordering: the new check sits after the pre-existing capability-level realization check and before authority, so incompatible -> unavailable under all three authority states; this is the established convention, not a new inversion, but it means denied+incompatible now reports unavailable rather than refused -- an inherited-ordering observation for the ordering owner. Two scope notes, neither a defect in this commit: (1) this commit added no tests -- 2 of the 3 promoted D1-006 gates were already green from bc226dc, so D1-006 must not be read later as 'three new tests written'; the locked gate is also a permissive negative (allows unavailable/needs-choice/unknown/refused) rather than asserting unavailable plus its reason. (2) The fix is provider-only and ignores freshness, while the module's canonical compatibleAccounts (src/world.ts:92-95) also requires freshness==='fresh': on W3 the stale account yields compatibleAccounts=[] yet validateInterpretation returns needs-consent, and ready under authority=allowed. That is pre-existing, not introduced here, and belongs to D1-016/D1-017, not to D1-006's closure.

review.head: ee1be8a11d71
review.note: ACCEPT (independent, adversarial). Verified at HEAD 76fe02b, working tree clean for the reviewed files. Gate hardening is real: both original D1-016 assertions are retained verbatim and four gates now run under a forced authority=allowed World (b-world.gate.test.ts:72-86), so the verdict is decided by freshness rather than by needs-consent. Discrimination proven by mutation, not by reading: deleting the single freshness line (validate.ts:130) from a /tmp copy turns EXACTLY one gate red - 'W3 stale Account is refused for freshness even when authority allows it' - while the pre-existing 'W3 stale Account can never yield a READY command' stays green, which is the direct confirmation of dev-trv-1110's finding that the original gate was vacuous. Positive control is one-factor: with the authority map merged identically in both arms, W3-stale -> needs-info ('account: \account:claude-work\ is stale, not fresh') and W3-fresh -> ready. The blocker is load-bearing end to end, not just a label: dispatch commit is rejected NOT_READY needs-info for the stale Account and granted only for the fresh control; granting consent does not revive it. Freshness is read in exactly one readiness place (validate.ts:130) and precedes realization and authority (validate.ts:131-137); observable proof of the ordering is that W3 at its authored consent-required authority now returns needs-info/stale rather than needs-consent. No bypass exists: commit is gated by validation() (session.ts:67-68) and project.ts:101 reports ready only from an accepted commit; executeVirtual is still a stub. RESIDUAL GAPS (recorded, not blocking): (1) no gate pins the freshness-before-authority ORDERING - a one-line assertion that fixture W3 (consent-required) returns needs-info with a /stale/ reason would lock COUNCIL's requirement down; (2) the gate would also pass if freshness were implemented as a compile-path blocker in unresolvedFor, so it pins behaviour but not the architectural placement inside the one READY law; (3) spec.json still declares D1-016 surface as src/world.ts + worlds/, while the implementation now lives in validate.ts (D1-005's file) - a provenance/surface mismatch worth reconciling. Freshness verdict state 'needs-info' is a reasonable, internally consistent label here: contract.ts:121 has no 'stale' verdict, and the compile path already mapped its 'stale' unresolved reason to needs-info, so the two paths agree.

review.head: fa0401427d32
review.note: ACCEPT (independent, adversarial, mutation-tested; label dev-trv-d14329b). Prior reject dev-trv-d14329 is answered on every disarm it named. Scope: 2aabfed (gate), f0f30a0 (fix), 3917d73 (projections). HEAD advanced 3917d73 -> fa04014 mid-review; the two intervening commits touch neither experimental/d1 nor experimental/ratchet, so D1-017 code+spec are byte-identical to 3917d73. GATE (upheld): name 'an explicit unknown target never resolves to another Account, even with authority allowed' is byte-identical across 2aabfed^/2aabfed/HEAD; all five D1-017 gates retained, none renamed or removed (b-world.gate.test.ts:88,93,101,121,129). 2aabfed is +6/-2, strictly stricter: only the loop's string list grew, every assertion at :110-117 is retained. SPEC_CHANGE is real: 2aabfed recorded it in ratchet.lock.json and the on-disk file digest sha256:ebc1758... matches the recorded 'to' exactly, so check correctly emits no SPEC_CHANGED -- the prior reviewer's governance gap is closed. CODE (upheld): f0f30a0 is confined to omega-baseline/experimental/d1/src/compile.ts and, inside it, to unheldRoute (compile.ts:500-510); 3917d73 regenerates only .project/evidence/d1-ratchet.json and .project/ratchet/D1-BOARD.md. VERIFY: RATCHET_MODE=probe bun run ratchet verify D1-017 -> 'D1-017 PROVEN', all 5 gates [promoted], exit 0. STATUS: bun run ratchet status --probe -> probe 0137952be72a (45/85 green); DONE 14 / PROVEN 15 / OPEN 11 / BLOCKED 37 / REGRESSED 0. CHECK: exit 0, 'check ok (5 warning(s))', all five PROMOTE_PENDING are unrelated to D1-017. NO REGRESSION: full-suite gate outcome set (pass/fail per gate, 125 lines) is byte-identical between 46de059 and HEAD -- zero newly-red, zero newly-green. MUTATION (each on a disposable /tmp worktree, all removed): (a) compile.ts reverted to f0f30a0^ -> gate FAILS at b-world.gate.test.ts:110 (Expected: not 'ready'). (b) unheldRoute made to REQUIRE a quote token -> gate FAILS, same line: the unquoted form retargets. (c) unheldRoute disabled (return null) -> gate FAILS, same line. So all three prior disarmings -- trailing ! ? -, trailing clause, quote after route -- are each independently load-bearing and discriminated against by a red gate. PROBES (authority forced allowed via fixture spread + prompt.send@1=allowed; W4 unless noted; account never filled): every one of the 7 gate strings returns state=needs-info, account=null, provider=null, unresolved=[account=unknown, options=[]], reason 'account: "gemini" grounded to no account' ('the team' for the multi-word case) -- needs-info, never ready, never claude-work. Also: 'send hello to Gemini.' needs-info/no fill; 'send hello to Gemini, please' needs-info/no fill; 'send hello to Gemini "x"' needs-info/no fill; 'send hello to work claude!' ready/account:claude-work (correct, held route); 'send hello to work claude' ready/account:claude-work; W1 'send hello' ready/account:claude-work (unchanged default fill); W2 'send hello to claude!' needs-choice, provider:provider:claude, options=[account:claude-personal, account:claude-work] (ambiguity preserved, D1 never picks); 'send \'tell it to Gemini\' to work claude' ready/account:claude-work with prompt exactly 'tell it to Gemini' -- quoted payload untouched and never retargets; 'send \'x\' about the outage' ready/account:claude-work with prompt 'x' -- 'about' correctly not a target preposition. ZERO false negatives among the gate strings and their near neighbours. RESIDUALS (recorded, follow-up warranted, NOT grounds for rejection -- each is byte-identical at bd241e2, 46de059 and HEAD, i.e. neither introduced nor closed by f0f30a0): (R1) params.prompt still carries the route words when a non-word token follows the route: 'send hello to Gemini!' -> prompt 'hello to Gemini!' (not 'hello'). Root cause compile.ts:525 -- payloadOf returns a CONTIGUOUS text.slice from the first unconsumed token to the last, so an unconsumed trailing '!' extends the slice back over the consumed route. It also hits HELD routes: 'send hello to work claude!' is READY with prompt 'hello to work claude!'. Confirmed pre-existing and unchanged by this fix. (R2) multi-recipient utterances still fill: 'send hello to Gemini via work claude', 'send hello to work claude and to Gemini', 'send hello to Gemini, then to work claude' all return ready/account:claude-work with the unheld target silently dropped. Root cause compile.ts:155 -- unheldRoute runs only when grounded.mention === null, so once the grounder finds the held 'work claude' the unheld mention is never read. Identical at bd241e2 and 46de059. The gate NAME still claims 'never', which is broader than the single-recipient behaviour exercised; per 'no rename hiding gaps' the right follow-up is an explicit gate for the multi-recipient class, not a rename. (R3) fail-safe false positive, documented in the code comment at compile.ts:489-499 and unchanged by f0f30a0: 'on' is a TARGET_PREP, so 'send hello on Monday' refuses as unknown target needs-info/monday, and 'send hello to Gemini on Friday' refuses on 'friday'. Fails safe, never retargets, but it narrows the phrase surface with no gate pinning it. (R4) COVERAGE GAP, new evidence: the gate is insensitive to mention CONTENT. Mutant (b') unheldRoute's word-run extended to the end of the utterance (terminators and all) stays GREEN. It degrades the mention to 'gemini !', 'gemini ?', 'gemini - thanks', 'gemini x', 'the team !' while the no-fill property still holds, so the directive is not violated -- but the gate asserts reason/options/account only (b-world.gate.test.ts:110-117) and never the mention string, so any future regression that keeps the decision and corrupts the mention would pass silently. A single expect on the mention text for 'the team' would close it. (R5) HEAD moved during review and the working tree carries pre-existing uncommitted .project/ edits from concurrent council/devops sessions; neither affects the D1-017 code or spec digest.

interpretation.ratchetModeGreen: the ratchet-mode gate suite (`bun run d1:gates`) exits green while open gates run as expected failures — it means open gaps are represented honestly and promoted gates have not regressed, NOT that the deliverable works

limitations: Gate results are claims about the code at the probed HEAD only.
A PROVEN task has promoted green gates but no independent review yet.
Fixture and simulated results are never live results.

Reviewer identity (`--by <label>`) is an auditable coordination label, not cryptographic proof that two labels are independent underlying actors; the engine enforces label separation, not actor independence (C2).
Ratchet-mode green (`d1:gates`) is not completion; only the probe-green frontier plus independent reviews, and finally the completion record, are (C4).
